explanation: Methenyl and formyl groups in one-carbon metabolism are derived from serine catabolism and from the catabolism of tryptophan and histidine.
keyConcept: Methenyl and formyl groups derive from serine, tryptophan, and histidine catabolism, feeding into purine and formyl-Met-tRNA synthesis.
modelAnswer: Two different sources of methenyl: (1) Serine catabolism - N5,N10-methylene THF (from serine via SHMT) can be oxidized to N5,N10-methenyl THF by serine hydroxymethyltransferase in reverse or by methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase (MTHFD). Methenyl THF is an intermediate in the conversion of formyl groups to methylene groups and vice versa. (2) Tryptophan catabolism - the kynurenine pathway produces N-formylkynurenine, which generates one-carbon units at the formyl and methenyl oxidation levels. Two different sources of formyl: (1) Histidine catabolism - the catabolism of L-histidine produces N-formimino glutamate, which transfers a formyl group to THF (generating N10-formyl THF) via the formiminotransferase reaction. (2) Purine ring biosynthesis - N10-formyl THF provides two separate formyl groups for the synthesis of the purine ring (at positions C2 and C8 of the purine nucleus). These formyl groups are transferred by transformylases (GAR transformylase and AICAR transformylase) during de novo purine synthesis. Additionally, mitochondrial protein synthesis requires formyl-methionine (fMet) for the initiator tRNA.

explanation: Sodium (Na+) influx through voltage-gated channels drives the rapid upstroke of the neuronal action potential. When threshold is reached, Nav1.5/1.2 channels open, causing rapid depolarization from -70 mV toward +30 mV.
keyConcept: Sodium ion influx through voltage-gated Na+ channels is responsible for the rapid depolarization phase of the action potential.

explanation: The resting membrane potential (approximately -70 mV in neurons) closely matches the equilibrium potential of K+ (approximately -90 mV) because the membrane at rest is most permeable to K+ via leak channels.
keyConcept: The resting membrane potential approximates the K+ equilibrium potential due to high resting K+ permeability.
